mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% in the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a paradoxical labor market signal, often preceding a sharp correction, and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals subpar economic expansion, which reduces corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% annualized for four consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.
